items.title: Hardware & Infrastructure Stocks Q2 Teardown: Super Micro (NASDAQ:SMCI) Vs The Rest
items.summary: The end of an earnings season can be a great time to discover new stocks and assess how companies are handling the current business environment. Let’s take a look at how Super Micro (NASDAQ:SMCI) and the rest of the hardware & infrastructure stocks fared in Q2.

items.title: SMCI Rises 29% Year to Date: Time to Buy, Sell or Hold the Stock?
items.summary: Super Micro Computer gains 29% YTD as record backlog, AI partnerships and rising shipments fuel growth, while improving margins add to its appeal.

items.title: HPE Cannot Build AI Servers Fast Enough. Is the Stock Still Cheap?
items.summary: HPE has more than doubled this year on an AI server backlog that management says demand is outpacing by multiples, yet the stock still trades at a low-teens forward multiple. Here is whether that gap is an opportunity or a warning sign.

items.title: Dell Is Now Up 20% in a Month: Take Profits, or Buy More?
items.summary: Dell stock has already surged nearly 300% in 2026, and this month added another 20% on top of a blowout earnings beat. The question facing shareholders now is whether the AI server trade still has runway or whether the easy money is already gone.

Lower yield pressure can make the future earnings of fast growing companies look more attractive, especially when management has significant skin in the game through insider ownership. This article highlights three high growth, high insider commitment US stocks from our screener and explains why each one could deserve a closer look now. items.title: Can VRT's UIG Deal Deepen Its AI Power Edge Over APH & SMCI?
items.summary: Vertiv's $1.45B UIG deal adds microgrid and behind-the-meter power capabilities, broadening its AI data-center infrastructure push.

items.title: Vertiv Stock Keeps Cooling Off. One Analyst Says a 100% Rally Is Coming
items.summary: Vertiv has quietly shed nearly a third of its value from its peak even as earnings beats pile up and estimates keep climbing higher. One analyst has a target so far above current prices it sounds almost absurd, but the operating data behind it is harder to dismiss than you might expect.

items.title: Dell Just Jumped 16% and One Strategist Says That Is the Whole Tech Argument Right Now
items.summary: Dell's 16% single-day surge gave one market strategist the proof he needed that AI spending is grounded in fundamentals, not hype. But a closer look at the margins hiding beneath that record backlog tells a more complicated story about who actually profits when customers buy AI servers.
